samples.summary: The gutter's own sanitization of the author name (the documented "don't trust the store" boundary) has no test
samples.evidence: `authorOfRange` calls `sanitizeDisplayName(best.author)` and the comment claims this is the DOM boundary that no store is trusted to have cleaned. Every span in blame-gutter.test.ts (lines 28-90) uses already-clean names ('ann','bob','') — deleting the `sanitizeDisplayName` call in authorOfRange would leave the whole notes suite green. The only tests of dirty names are in display-name.test.ts (the pure function), yorkie-note-store.test.ts (the Yorkie store's own read path) and remote-selection.test.ts (caret label); none exercises computeBlameLabels/BlameMarker with a name containing ‮, ​ or a 500-char name.

samples.summary: New authorship-through-undo/redo logic in MemNoteStore (and attribution survival across Yorkie undo/redo) is untested
samples.evidence: The diff adds `authors` to MemState, snapshots it in `currentState()`/`batch()` and restores it in `restore()`. packages/notes/src/store/memory.test.ts has no occurrence of 'author' (grep returned no matches) and blame-gutter.test.ts never undoes/redoes, so removing `this.authors = state.authors.slice()` from `restore()` — leaving blame labels stale/wrong after undo — breaks no test. Likewise yorkie-note-store.test.ts's undo/redo block (lines 60+) only asserts `getText()`, never `getAuthorSpans()` after undo/redo, so attribution behaviour across Yorkie's reverse ops is entirely uncovered.

samples.summary: Sanitize-on-write in editText is never exercised: the forged-name tests bypass editText
samples.evidence: `editText` writes `sanitizeDisplayName(this.localAuthorName()) ?? ''` into the run attribute. The tests that use dirty names (yorkie-note-store.test.ts:283-297) write the attribute directly via `root.content.edit(..., { a: 'a‮nd...' })`, never through `editText` with a dirty presence name, and the tests that do use `editText` (lines 193-215) set only clean presence names. Dropping the sanitize call on the write path fails nothing.

samples.summary: The `(self-reported)` hover title on the blame label is asserted nowhere
samples.evidence: `BlameMarker.toDOM` sets `span.title = `${label} (self-reported)``, described in the comment as deliberately qualifying an unverified claim. The only DOM assertion helper in blame-gutter.test.ts (`gutterLabels`, lines 21-25) reads `textContent` only; no test queries `.cm-noteBlameLabel` or `title`, so the qualification could silently disappear.

samples.summary: The documented gutter-ordering constraint (blame gutter left of line numbers) is untested
samples.evidence: blame-gutter.ts:12-14 and editor.ts:354-356 state the gutter must be registered before `basicSetup` so it renders left of `lineNumbers()`. No test inspects gutter order: grep for `cm-lineNumbers`/`cm-gutters`/`activeGutters` in packages/notes/src matches only the comment in blame-gutter.ts. Moving the compartment after `basicSetup` would flip the visual layout with every test still green, since `gutterLabels` scopes its query to `.cm-noteBlame`.

samples.summary: New persistence helpers and the React wiring for `showAuthors` have no tests
samples.evidence: `readShowAuthors`/`writeShowAuthors` (notes-settings.ts:45-51), the `useEffect` that pushes the preference into the editor (notes-view.tsx:153-156) and the toolbar checkbox (notes-toolbar.tsx:355-363) have no test files: the only test files under packages/frontend/src/app/notes are yorkie-note-store.test.ts and notes-undo-integration.test.ts (glob of that directory), and no test references readShowAuthors/writeShowAuthors (grep across packages). Consistent with the untested readViewMode/readKeymap precedent, hence minor, but the default-false-and-persist behaviour the doc comment promises is unverified — and frontend has no tsc lane either.

The function documents that anything not a positive finite number reads as `0`, but the added tests only cover a far-future number (line 245), an in-skew number (line 275) and normal `Date.now()` writes. No test writes `t: 'abc'`, `t: NaN`, `t: -1` or omits `t` while setting `a`, so the `typeof/isFinite/<= 0` guard could be deleted without failing anything (a string `t` would then flow straight into `at`).

finding.summary: The gutter's own sanitization of the author name (the documented "don't trust the store" boundary) has no test
finding.evidence: `authorOfRange` calls `sanitizeDisplayName(best.author)` and the comment claims this is the DOM boundary that no store is trusted to have cleaned. Every span in blame-gutter.test.ts (lines 28-90) uses already-clean names ('ann','bob','') — deleting the `sanitizeDisplayName` call in authorOfRange would leave the whole notes suite green. The only tests of dirty names are in display-name.test.ts (the pure function), yorkie-note-store.test.ts (the Yorkie store's own read path) and remote-selection.test.ts (caret label); none exercises computeBlameLabels/BlameMarker with a name containing ‮, ​ or a 500-char name.

verdict.reason: Verified: authorOfRange sanitizes at the gutter boundary (blame-gutter.ts:38-58) and BlameMarker.toDOM writes the label into textContent/title (109-120), but every author name in blame-gutter.test.ts is already clean ('ann','bob','cal',null,''), and sanitizeDisplayName is identity on those (display-name.ts:50-57), so deleting the call leaves the file green — including the '' -> ANONYMOUS_AUTHOR case (test lines 75-79), which passes either way. MemNoteStore stores localAuthor verbatim (memory.ts:100-131), so the gutter is the only strip point on that path, yet no test feeds it a dirty name (setLocalAuthor appears only at blame-gutter.test.ts:110,112,131,148,172, all clean). Searched wide for a counterexample and found none: repo-wide grep for computeBlameLabels/BlameMarker/cm-noteBlame/ANONYMOUS_AUTHOR/blame-gutter finds only the one test file; the dirty-name tests live in display-name.test.ts (pure function), yorkie-note-store.test.ts:280-297 (asserts getAuthorSpans, never renders the gutter) and remote-selection.test.ts:48-75 (caret label, and its store stub returns getAuthorSpans: () => []); note-sync.test.ts:19 also stubs spans empty; there is no e2e/Playwright notes suite and notes-undo-integration.test.ts has no author/blame coverage. A documented trust-boundary behavior shipped with zero test that could fail if it regressed — missing-test, in lane, blocking.

finding.summary: New authorship-through-undo/redo logic in MemNoteStore (and attribution survival across Yorkie undo/redo) is untested
finding.evidence: The diff adds `authors` to MemState, snapshots it in `currentState()`/`batch()` and restores it in `restore()`. packages/notes/src/store/memory.test.ts has no occurrence of 'author' (grep returned no matches) and blame-gutter.test.ts never undoes/redoes, so removing `this.authors = state.authors.slice()` from `restore()` — leaving blame labels stale/wrong after undo — breaks no test. Likewise yorkie-note-store.test.ts's undo/redo block (lines 60+) only asserts `getText()`, never `getAuthorSpans()` after undo/redo, so attribution behaviour across Yorkie's reverse ops is entirely uncovered.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: MemNoteStore snapshots and restores per-character authorship through undo/redo (memory.ts:150-158, 221-235), observable via getAuthorSpans (memory.ts:100-122), and nothing asserts it. memory.test.ts (132 lines read in full) never touches authorship, so removing `this.authors = state.authors.slice()` from restore() breaks no assertion. I looked well beyond the reviewer's searches: blame-gutter.test.ts is the only test calling setLocalAuthor and it never invokes undo/redo; yorkie-note-store.test.ts keeps its undo/redo block (60-181, getText/stack-depth/selection only) strictly disjoint from its author-spans block (183-308, no undo); and the most plausible hidden counterexample, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-undo-integration.test.ts, mounts the real store+view over Yorkie undo/redo yet asserts only getText() and undo-stack depth, never getAuthorSpans(). Remaining MemNoteStore consumers either ignore authorship (editor.test.ts) or stub getAuthorSpans to [] (note-sync.test.ts:19, remote-selection.test.ts:19). Repo-wide greps for setLocalAuthor/getAuthorSpans/noteBlame/showAuthors enumerate every authorship entry point, so the search is exhaustive rather than partial. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a real behavior with no meaningful test (major).
